clue.text: Leave chaps beginning to teach division

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to leave is to depart
chaps are men
first letter of 'teach'

explanation.surface: A school's staff are told to quit before starting to teach some division of their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' sounds like arithmetic to be taught, but it is the definition, read as a section of an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a section or branch of a larger organisation, such as a government or company.

clue.text: See fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: to go out with someone romantically, as in 'are you seeing anyone?'
second meaning: the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like an instruction pointing at fruit, but it is a definition in its own right: to see someone is to court them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for courting someone regularly and a noun for the palm tree's sweet sticky produce.

clue.text: Edge of boggy area to the north circumvented by saint

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
something circumvented is surrounded on all sides, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: a mire is a stretch of bog
St Peter the apostle

explanation.surface: The rim of a marsh to the north has been walked around by a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint' is not the usual ST here but a named apostle, split after his first letter to take in the upturned bog.
explanation.definitionFit: The perimeter is the outer boundary or border of an area, which is what its edge is.

clue.text: Philosopher‘s rent decreases, oddly

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters end up in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A thinker's rent strangely goes down, as if a landlord has turned generous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters, but that gives far too few; here it signals a rearrangement of all thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Descartes was the seventeenth-century French thinker famous for 'I think, therefore I am'.

clue.text: Encountered that guy purchasing an essential element of natural gas

indicators.note: purchasing means getting hold of something, so one piece takes another inside it

blocks.note: to have encountered someone is to have met them
the pronoun for a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bumping into a man who is buying the key ingredient of the gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchasing' reads as shopping, but it means gripping: HE holds AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is the main component of natural gas, making up most of its volume as burned in homes.

clue.text: Currently, that woman’s on ecstasy in remote place

definitions.note: used loosely, as in 'the middle of nowhere'

blocks.note: currently means at present
the pronoun for a woman
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman is high on drugs somewhere far from anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a standard crossword abbreviation from the drug's street name.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In the middle of nowhere' describes an isolated spot, so the word stands for some faraway unknown location.

clue.text: Old South American‘s tiny scar discovered

indicators.note: dis-covered means having its covers taken off, so each word loses its outside letters

blocks.note: the inner pair of 'tiny'
the inner pair of 'scar'

explanation.surface: An archaeologist uncovers an ancient Peruvian with a small scar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as found, but split as dis-covered it means stripped of the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas were the native people whose empire ruled the Andes until the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: New operatic song raised money in Nigeria

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something lifts it to read bottom to top

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A new opera number brought in funds in Lagos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised money' suggests fundraising; 'raised' belongs to the wordplay and 'money in Nigeria' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The naira is the national currency unit of Nigeria, divided into a hundred kobo.

clue.text: Deals with representatives detaining mere criminal

indicators.note: to detain is to hold someone in, so one piece goes inside another
criminal suggests something crooked or wrong, so these letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: agents act as representatives for others
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plea bargains struck by lawyers who are holding a petty offender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun for the person detained, but it is the anagram signal for the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deals are arrangements settled between parties, which is what agreements are; both are plural nouns.

clue.text: Go around this person’s Italian city

indicators.note: going around something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a go in a game is a turn
this person is the setter, so I

explanation.surface: A tourist is told to take a tour of their own city in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go around' reads as a single phrase meaning tour; split, 'Go' is TURN and 'around' wraps it round 'this person', the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is the capital of Piedmont in northern Italy, home of Fiat and Juventus.

clue.text: Bank securing personal credit for former news presenter?

indicators.note: securing something means holding it firmly, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: a tier is a bank, as in a row of seats or a bank of switches
your own is personal to you
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A bank lends money to a retired newsreader on personal credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' tempts a financial reading, but it means a tier or row; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Before newspapers and broadcasts, a bellman walked the streets shouting public announcements, so he presented the news.

clue.text: Family established in Cambridgeshire city nursing daughter in secret

indicators.note: nursing something means holding it close, so one piece takes another into its middle

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family group
EST is the abbreviation for established, seen on shop signs
taken as written
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family settled in a fenland city is secretly looking after a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is an English cathedral city near Cambridge; the daughter is tucked in right after the family, inside the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something clandestinely means doing it covertly, hidden from view; both are adverbial phrases.

clue.text: Intervene and think carefully, having no time

indicators.note: having none of something means it is left out of the word

blocks.note: to meditate is to think deeply
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Advice to anyone stepping into a dispute: stop and reflect, though there is no time.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the T out of MEDITATE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to step in between disputing parties to help them reach a settlement.

clue.text: Cognisant of fighting in A&E

definitions.note: the answer is used with 'of' too: aware of

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: taken as written, letters only
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Staff are well informed about brawls breaking out in the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department (Accident and Emergency); here only its letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognisant and aware are synonyms meaning having knowledge or realisation of something.

clue.text: Recyclable material was flipping dear? A salesman’s upset

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end
in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
pet is a term of endearment, like dear
taken as written
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: Recycling was flipping expensive, and a salesman is unhappy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping dear' reads as British slang for very expensive; 'flipping' is the reversal sign and 'dear' is PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Discarded paper is collected and pulped for reuse, making it a common example of recyclable stuff.

clue.text: To an extent, part is terrifying for performer

indicators.note: only to an extent means partially, so just a stretch of the following letters is used

blocks.note: runs across the three words

explanation.surface: A role that is partly scary for the actor taking it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like a theatrical role tied to the performer, but it just supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer, such as a singer or dancer, on stage.

clue.text: Need AGM to change final section

indicators.note: changing the letters means reorganising them into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A company needs its annual general meeting to amend the last part of something.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGM is an annual general meeting, but here it is just three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess and by extension elsewhere, the endgame is the closing stage of a match or process.

clue.text: Some fear gent in African country

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only a portion, so a run of its letters is taken

blocks.note: runs across the words, ending on the first letter of the last

explanation.surface: Some man is afraid while in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African country' looks like the definition, but the answer is in South America; the A of 'African' ends the hidden run and 'country' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a large South American nation, capital Buenos Aires.

clue.text: Royal Navy notice breaking also in storm

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: too means also
RN is the abbreviation for Royal Navy
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A naval announcement goes out during bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' sounds like news breaking, but here two pieces break into a third word together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating column of wind, one of the fiercest kinds of tempest.

clue.text: Plant king’s daughter is captivated by over and over again

indicators.note: someone captivated is held captive, so this piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over, given twice

explanation.surface: A princess is enchanted by the same plant time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's daughter' is not a generic princess but Regan from King Lear; 'over and over again' supplies one O on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of the mint family, used in Italian and Greek cooking.

clue.text: Understanding current things badly

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so these letters are out of order

blocks.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grasping current affairs poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective for things, but it is the symbol I used in electrical formulas.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep, intuitive grasp of a situation, so it is a kind of comprehension.

clue.text: First one egg, one with endless salt

indicators.note: without its ends, a word keeps only the letters between them

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a nit is a louse's egg
the Roman numeral for one again
the middle pair of letters of 'salt'

explanation.surface: A recipe step: start with one egg, then one more with a little salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' removes both ends here, not just the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means occurring at the beginning, so it is a straightforward synonym of first as an adjective.

clue.text: Hint about maintaining the French braid

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
to maintain something is to keep hold of it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a tip is a hint
la is French for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: A hairdressing tip about keeping a French-style braid in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French braid' is a real hairstyle, but 'the French' gives LA and 'braid' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait is hair or rope woven from three or more interlaced strands, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Questioned male leaving with face covered

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it drops out of the word

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
a masked face is covered

explanation.surface: A man was interrogated while leaving in a mask.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing M from MASKED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked and questioned both mean put a query to someone, as past-tense verbs.

clue.text: Rebellion without singular issue

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: sedition is incitement to rebel against authority
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: An uprising with no particular cause behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' reads as a matter or problem, but here it is a printed issue of a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition of a newspaper or magazine is one published number of it, the same as an issue.

clue.text: Duck has drink by lake

blocks.note: tea is a drink
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A water bird takes a sip at the side of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' could be a verb, but it is the noun: a kind of bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling bird of the genus Anas, one of the commonest wildfowl species.

clue.text: Unorthodox pianist entertaining a king from Asian country

indicators.note: unorthodox means unconventional, so the letters are arranged in a nonstandard way
a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An unconventional musician from South Asia plays for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged PIANIST splits after its P to take in A and K.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people or things belonging to Pakistan, the nation between India and Afghanistan.

clue.text: Former priest from the east cast out

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left

blocks.note: ex means former
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A one-time cleric from the Orient was expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is the crossword's favourite priest, from the Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them from their homeland, so the verb matches expelled.

clue.text: Naked women getting married travel by horse

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the outer letters come off

blocks.note: women getting married are brides; strip the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Women at their wedding ride horses unclothed, like Lady Godiva.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase gives BRIDES, then 'Naked' strips its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to be carried on horseback, a verb that matches the definition phrase.

clue.text: Everyone follows strangely lovely British sport

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of the normal way, so the letters are rearranged
following means coming after, so this piece is placed at the end

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for British
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everybody is a fan of an oddly lovely British game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British sport' looks like the definition, but B comes from 'British' and only 'sport' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Volleyball is a team game in which a ball is hit over a high net by hand.
